clinician.trajectory_summary: A 30-year-old man presented with 4-day dry cough, exertional dyspnoea, severe lower limb and scrotal edema, disseminated pigmented rash, extensive non-tender cervical lymphadenopathy, and marked cachexia. HIV serology was positive with significant immunosuppression (CD4 count 116 cells/μL, viral load 87,272 copies/mL). A CT-guided biopsy of an iliac crest bone lesion confirmed Kaposi's sarcoma via spindle cell proliferation positive for CD34 and HHV-8. Clinical examination supported disseminated disease with multiple organ involvement. This confirmed widely disseminated HIV-associated Kaposi's sarcoma.
